previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted with fever, abdominal pain, and back pain, concerning for pyelonephritis and acute on chronic kidney injury, with a creatinine of 7.2. Imaging and a loopogram revealed a left ureteral obstruction causing severe hydronephrosis. A left percutaneous nephrostomy was placed for drainage, leading to improvement in renal function. Urine cultures grew Pseudomonas aeruginosa and Enterococcus, prompting a switch from meropenem to gentamicin. He completed a two-week course of IV antibiotics via a PICC line, which was removed prior to discharge. A nephroureteral stent was placed to maintain drainage, and the patient was transitioned to oral pain medications. He was discharged home in stable condition with plans for urology follow-up and stent exchange in three months.

INDICATION:  ___ year old man with urosepsis and NU stent (growing pseudomonas
from urine and blood, need exchange of percutaneous NU stent.

COMPARISON:  Left percutaneous nephrostomy to NU stent exchange from
___.

TECHNIQUE:   OPERATORS: Dr. ___ (radiology resident) and Dr. ___
___ (interventional radiology attending) performed the procedure. The
attending, Dr. ___ was present and supervising throughout the procedure.
Dr. ___ radiologist, personally supervised the trainee during
the key components of the procedure and reviewed and agreed with the trainee's
findings.
ANESTHESIA: Moderate sedation was provided by administrating divided doses of
100mcg of fentanyl and 2 mg of midazolam throughout the total intra-service
time of 10 minutes during which the patient's hemodynamic parameters were
continuously monitored by an independent trained radiology nurse. 1% lidocaine
was injected in the skin and subcutaneous tissues overlying the access site.
MEDICATIONS: Fentanyl, Versed, lidocaine.
CONTRAST: 30 ml of Optiray contrast.
FLUOROSCOPY TIME AND DOSE: 2.9 minutes, 587 cGy-cm2

PROCEDURE:  1. 8 ___  nephroureteral stent exchange.

PROCEDURE DETAILS: Following the discussion of the risks, benefits and
alternatives to the procedure, written informed consent was obtained from the
patient. The patient was then brought to the angiography suite and placed
supine on the exam table. A pre-procedure time-out was performed per ___
protocol. The tube site was prepped and draped in the usual sterile fashion.

Position of the existing left NU stent was verified by antegrade injection of
Optiray. Intrarenal position of the existing pigtail catheter in the
collecting system of the left kidney as well as the distal pigtail within the
ileal conduit were confirmed. An antegrade nephrogram was not performed due to
ongoing infection and no current plan for intervention.  The catheter was then
cut, and ___ wire was advanced into the ileal conduit. The existing
catheter was removed. A 8 ___, 22 cm nephroureteral stent was placed under
real-time fluoroscopic visualization. The loops of the catheter were formed
within the ileal conduit and the left renal pelvis and locked. Position of the
newly placed catheter was verified by injection of contrast. The catheter was
sutured to the skin. A StatLock was applied to secure the catheter from
traction, and sterile dressing was applied to the skin.

The patient tolerated the procedure well and there were no immediate
post-procedure complications.

FINDINGS: 

1. Moderate to severe left hydronephrosis.
2. Successful exchange of an existing 8 ___ nephroureteral stent for a new
8 ___ nephroureteral stent.

IMPRESSION: 

1.  Successful exchange of a 8 ___ nephroureteral stent on the left.
2. Nephrogram was not performed due to ongoing infection and no immediate plan
for intervention.

RECOMMENDATION:  1.  Given manipulation, nephroureteral stent is currently
attached to a bag. Catheter may be capped later today or tomorrow in
preparation for discharge.
2. Routine exchange of nephroureteral stent in 3 months. At that time, we will
perform nephrogram to determine need for further intervention.
